This is partially addressed by #23650 — a minimal `session.turn.completed` event (+9 lines, 2 files). It enables post-turn plugins like [ScarletWitch](https://github.com/xbjpku/ScarletWitch), a filesystem sandbox that shows a COW review dialog after each turn. Happy to adjust based on feedback.

Related: #23650 adds a complementary `session.turn.completed` event that fires *after* the turn ends (for post-turn plugins like sandbox review dialogs), vs `session.stopping` which fires *before* (for loop re-entry). Different use case but same lifecycle area — +9 lines, zero breaking changes.

I experienced this too (reproducibly) with a local model and a 16K context limit.

However, when I upped the model’s context window to 128K last week (both in Llama.cpp and the limit in the OpenCode config), the issue was gone immediately and never came back.

This issue might be related to existing issues about shell PATH/environment not being inherited by the OpenCode server process. Please check:
- #4968: Shell sessions losing $PATH value from parent shell
- #17792: [FEATURE]: Unify shell initialization behavior between user shell and agent bash tool
- #15195: Desktop app does not inherit full PATH from shell environment (closed)

Since your OpenCode server runs as a Systemd unit, it likely does not source your `.bashrc`, so `PATH` entries set there (like Node.js/npm paths) are not available to the bash tool. You may be able to work around this by setting the `PATH` explicitly in the Systemd unit's `Environment=` or `EnvironmentFile=` directive, or by configuring a login shell in your OpenCode bash tool settings.

- #20235: Requests the same GitHub Copilot auto model routing feature, with detailed context about the API endpoints and current limitations

```
Feature hasn't been suggested before.

    I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

Describe the enhancement you want to request

I would like to request a feature that automatically applies Google Translate between user-facing text and the prompts sent to the API.
```

Using google translate for translating is not a good idea, because this is an additional dependency and will not work, if google is not available or if you use opencode in an secured/offline environment with local models.

#23077 is the better idea: simply add an addition model-call to translate the Input (and if relay needed) the output of the model too, by adding an additional model call, because all the large language models are able to deliver great translations from/to "models favorite language".

You can try browsing skills here https://skills.sh

For skill creator, you can also add it as skill (check https://skills.sh/anthropics/skills/skill-creator). By simply running the command in that page:

```sh
npx skills add https://github.com/anthropics/skills --skill skill-creator
```

You can choose whether to add the skill to project or global scope in the prompt. And by default, the added skill is available for OpenCode too.

> This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
> 
>     * [[FEATURE]: Support automatic translation between the UI and API for prompts and responses #16761](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/16761): Feature request for automatic translation between UI and API for prompts/responses — describes essentially the same concept of translating non-English prompts to English before sending to the model
> 
>     * [How to globally set the language for model thinking and answering #9610](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/9610): Question about globally setting the language for model thinking and answering — related discussion

My question is not duplicate to #16761, because #16761  is a request to use "google translate" for translating all prompts. Using a external Service is not a good idea, because this will not work, if you work offline and/or google is not available on the system. AND translating the prompt into the models language (mostly English) will work with the most models. So you don't need to build a dependency to an other/external system/service.

Also, #9610 will do something different: the issue is about changing the models language, meaning how the model will "think" and answer. But, this is the point: the result of the model is much better, if you not force the model to think and work in an other language than the language where the Model was build on.

The results are much better, if the model works in "his own language" and only output/input are translated by an additional call to the model.
